verses.text: This na Jesus Christ’s family record: David’s son, Abraham’s son. Roots go way back, fam. 🌱
Abraham fathered Isaac. Isaac fathered Jacob. Jacob fathered Judah and his brothers. The family line dey roll, no cap. 🌳
Judah fathered Perez and Zerah through Tamar. Perez fathered Hezron; Hezron fathered Ram. Family tree dey branch out, abeg. 🌿
Ram fathered Amminadab. Amminadab fathered Nahshon. Nahshon fathered Salmon. Next name, next generation. 📜
Salmon fathered Boaz through Rahab. Boaz fathered Obed through Ruth. Obed fathered Jesse. Family tree still growing. ✨
Jesse fathered King David. David the king fathered Solomon through the woman who had been Uriah’s wife. 👑
Solomon fathered Rehoboam. Rehoboam fathered Abijah. Abijah fathered Asa. The line carries on. 🔁
Asa fathered Jehoshaphat. Jehoshaphat fathered Joram. Joram fathered Uzziah. Next names in the family chain. ⛓️
Uzziah fathered Jotham. Jotham fathered Ahaz. Ahaz fathered Hezekiah. One generation hands off to the next. 🙌
Hezekiah fathered Manasseh. Manasseh fathered Amon. Amon fathered Josiah. The family record keeps rolling. 📖
Josiah fathered Jechoniah and his brothers when the people were exiled to Babylon. A hard turn in the story. 🧳
After the exile to Babylon, Jechoniah fathered Shealtiel; Shealtiel fathered Zerubbabel. The line kept going after exile. 🌅
Zerubbabel fathered Abiud. Abiud fathered Eliakim. Eliakim fathered Azor. Another generation, another handoff. 📝
Azor fathered Zadok. Zadok fathered Achim. Achim fathered Eliud. The names keep moving down the line. ➡️
Eliud fathered Eleazar. Eleazar fathered Matthan. Matthan fathered Jacob. The family record rolls on. 📜
Jacob fathered Joseph, Mary’s husband. Mary gave birth to Jesus, who is called Christ. ✨
So, count it: Abraham to David—14 generations; David to the exile in Babylon—14; and the exile to Christ—14. Three sets, each fourteen. 🔢
Here’s how Jesus Christ was born: Mary was engaged to Joseph, but before they came together, she was found pregnant through the Holy Spirit.
Joseph, her husband, was a righteous man. He didn’t want to make her a public spectacle, so he planned to quietly break the engagement.

While Joseph was thinking it over, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and said, “Joseph, son of David, don’t be afraid to take Mary as your wife. The child conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit.
She will give birth to a son. Name him Jesus, because he will save his people from their sins.”
All this happened to fulfill what the Lord had spoken through the prophet:
“Look, the virgin will become pregnant and give birth to a son. They will call him Immanuel”—which means, “God with us.”
Joseph woke up and did what the Lord’s angel commanded him: he took Mary as his wife.
But he did not sleep with her until she gave birth to her firstborn son. Joseph named him Jesus.
